title: Coefficient tensor product commutes with homogeneous localized module pieces
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ a commutative unital graded ring with a unital map $R\to A_0$, and $M=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}M_i$ a graded $A$-module, meaning $A_nM_i\subseteq M_{n+i}$. Put $C=S\otimes_RA$, graded by $C_n=S\otimes_RA_n$, and $N=S\otimes_RM$, graded by $N_i=S\otimes_RM_i$, with $C$-action $(s\otimes a)(t\otimes x)=st\otimes ax$. Fix $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, and put $f_S=1\otimes f$. Write $M_f$ and $N_{f_S}$ for module localization at the powers of $f$ and $f_S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For every integer $j$, let $(M_f)_j$ be the $R$-submodule of $M_f$ consisting of fractions $x/f^m$ with $m\geq0$ and $x\in M_{md+j}$, and define $(N_{f_S})_j$ similarly. Equality is the ordinary module-localization relation, so $x/f^m=y/f^n$ if and only if $f^k(f^nx-f^my)=0$ for some $k\geq0$. The displayed subsets are $R$- and $S$-modules respectively, with addition by a common denominator. The rule
$$\lambda_{M,f,j}:S\otimes_R(M_f)_j\xrightarrow{\sim}(N_{f_S})_j,\qquad s\otimes(x/f^m)\longmapsto(s\otimes x)/f_S^m$$
defines an isomorphism of $S$-modules. No flatness, finite generation, boundedness of the grading of $M$, or non-zero-divisor hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

proof.text: Fix $j\in\mathbf Z$ and put $D_m=M_{md+j}$ for $m\in\mathbf N$, with transition $t_{nm}:D_m\to D_n$, $x\mapsto f^{n-m}x$ for $m\le n$. These are $R$-linear and satisfy $t_{pm}=t_{pn}t_{nm}$ because powers add. The maps $u_m:D_m\to H=(M_f)_j$, $x\mapsto x/f^m$, form a cocone: $f^{n-m}x/f^n=x/f^m$ by the localization relation. Addition of fractions with denominators $m,n$ takes place at the common stage $m+n$, and scalar multiplication changes only the numerator; thus $H$ is the stated $R$-submodule.

source.place: Tag 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj), standard-open calculation, agent-supplied graded-module refinement; fraction relation from algebra.tex Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module).

proof.text: This cocone is a colimit. Given compatible $R$-linear maps $v_m:D_m\to P$, define $v(x/f^m)=v_m(x)$. If $x/f^m=y/f^n$, choose $k\ge0$ with $f^{k+n}x=f^{k+m}y$; both sides lie in $D_{k+m+n}$. Compatibility gives $v_m(x)=v_{k+m+n}(f^{k+n}x)=v_{k+m+n}(f^{k+m}y)=v_n(y)$. Hence $v$ is well-defined. Passing to a common denominator proves additivity; $v_m(rx)=rv_m(x)$ proves $R$-linearity. Every fraction comes from some $u_m$, proving uniqueness. Apply the identical construction to $N$ and $f_S$: with $E_m=N_{md+j}$, transitions $y\mapsto f_S^{n-m}y$, and $w_m(y)=y/f_S^m$, $H^\prime=(N_{f_S})_j$ is a colimit of $E_m$ as $R$-modules and also as $S$-modules. Here the test cocones may be $R$-linear or $S$-linear respectively, so no claim that restriction of scalars preserves colimits is needed.

source.place: Tag 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj), standard-open calculation, agent-supplied graded-module refinement; fraction relation from algebra.tex Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module).

proof.text: By the tensor-colimit theorem with fixed module $S$, and the balanced interchange $x\otimes s\leftrightarrow s\otimes x$, $S\otimes_R H$ with legs $q_m=1_S\otimes u_m$ is a colimit of $S\otimes_R D_m$ in $R$-modules. The specified tensor grading identifies $S\otimes_R D_m$ with $E_m$ by $\beta_m(s\otimes x)=s\otimes x$. These identifications intertwine transitions: $\beta_n(s\otimes f^{n-m}x)=f_S^{n-m}\beta_m(s\otimes x)$, first on pure tensors by the stated $C$-action and then on sums. There is no injectivity assumption on tensoring arbitrary inclusions here: each $M_i\hookrightarrow M$ is split by its grading projection, and tensoring this retraction identity still gives a retraction. Thus the displayed $N_i=S\otimes_RM_i$ really are the indicated submodules. The two colimit properties now supply inverse $R$-linear maps between $S\otimes_RH$ and $H^\prime$: the forward map has legs $w_m\beta_m$, and its inverse has legs $q_m\beta_m^{-1}$. Their composites fix all colimit legs and are identities by uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits); the transition and split-inclusion calculations are the agent-supplied module refinement of constructions.tex Tag 01N2.

proof.text: Call the forward equivalence $\lambda$. Its defining equation $\lambda q_m=w_m\beta_m$ gives $\lambda(s\otimes(x/f^m))=(s\otimes x)/f_S^m$. For $t\in S$, this formula gives $\lambda(ts\otimes(x/f^m))=t\lambda(s\otimes(x/f^m))$. Such pure tensors generate $S\otimes_RH$, so additivity proves $S$-linearity, and the bijection is an $S$-module isomorphism. All steps use fraction equality by multiplication with a power, never cancellation or exactness of tensoring; they apply equally when $f$ or $f_S$ is nilpotent, and for every integer $j$.
